Anab
AY-nab
proper noun
Hebrew Anab, “grape” or “place of grapes,” a town in the hill country of Judah.

📖 Biblical Definition

Anab was a town in the mountainous part of the inheritance of Judah, named in the roll of the hill-country cities of their allotment: “And Arab, and Dumah, and Eshean, and Janum, and Bethtappuah” — and among the towns, “And Anab” (Jos 15:50). It is remembered chiefly as one of the cities from which Joshua cut off the Anakim, the giant race whose great stature had so terrified the spies in the days of Moses. For when Joshua had taken the whole land, “at that time came Joshua, and cut off the Anakims from the mountains, from Hebron, from Debir, from Anab, and from all the mountains of Judah, and from all the mountains of Israel: Joshua destroyed them utterly with their cities” (Jos 11:21). Thus the very giants whom Israel had feared, saying they were as grasshoppers in their sight, were driven out and destroyed by the LORD through His servant Joshua; and Anab, once a stronghold of the Anakim, was given into the inheritance of Judah. The name Anab, “grape,” recalls the fruitful highlands near Hebron whence the spies had brought the great cluster of grapes from the brook of Eshcol. Anab stands as a witness that the LORD is mightier than the giants that affright His people; the strongholds that seemed impregnable He casts down, and gives His people the inheritance He has promised, though the sons of Anak stood in the way.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A town in the hill country of Judah from which Joshua cut off the Anakim and gave to the inheritance of Judah.

expand to see more

ANAB, a town in the hill country of Judah (Jos 15:50).

It was a stronghold of the Anakim, the race of giants.

Joshua cut off the Anakim from Anab and the mountains of Judah (Jos 11:21).

Its name signifies “grape” or “place of grapes.”

It was given into the inheritance of the tribe of Judah.

📖 Key Scripture

Jos 11:21 — "And at that time came Joshua, and cut off the Anakims from the mountains, from Hebron, from Debir, from Anab, and from all the mountains of Judah, and from all the mountains of Israel: Joshua destroyed them utterly with their cities."

Jos 15:50 — "And Anab, and Eshtemoh, and Anim,"

Jos 11:22 — "There was none of the Anakims left in the land of the children of Israel: only in Gaza, in Gath, and in Ashdod, there remained."

Jos 15:13 — "And unto Caleb the son of Jephunneh he gave a part among the children of Judah, according to the commandment of the LORD to Joshua, even the city of Arba the father of Anak, which city is Hebron."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A place of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; it witnesses to the LORD’s faithfulness in casting down the giants that affright His people.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is God’s faithfulness in giving the land, casting down even the giants the spies had feared. Anab was a stronghold of the Anakim, the great race whose stature had once made Israel say they were as grasshoppers; yet Joshua cut off the Anakim from Anab and all the mountains of Judah, and the city fell into the inheritance. What seemed impossible to unbelief the LORD performed; the giants that affrighted the ten spies were no match for the God who fought for His people.

The casting down of the Anakim from Anab typifies the believer’s inheritance and warfare in Christ, the greater Joshua. The strongholds and giants that stand between the saint and his promised rest are not too great for the Lord, who goes before His people to dispossess them. As Caleb, who wholly followed the LORD, drove the sons of Anak from Hebron, so the believer who trusts his God overcomes the powers that would bar him from the inheritance, for greater is He that is in us than the giants of the land.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The name means “grape” or “place of grapes,” borne by a hill town once held by the Anakim.

Anab — Hebrew Anab, “grape” or “place of grapes.”

It lay in the hill country of Judah near Hebron.

It was a stronghold of the Anakim.

Joshua cut off the Anakim from it.

It was given into the inheritance of Judah.

Usage

"Like Anab, the LORD casts down the giants that affright His people and gives them the promised land."

"Anab teaches that what seems impossible to unbelief the LORD performs for those who follow Him wholly."

"The greater Joshua drives out every power that bars the saint from his inheritance in Christ."
